input.quote: IN NO EVENT SHALL TRUELINK'S LIABILITY FOR ANY MATTER ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11 THIS AGREEMENT (OTHER THAN DUE TO A BREACH RESULTING FROM TRUELINK'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE OR WILLFUL MISCONDUCT) EXCEED THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD.
input.rationale: The only cap language in the Agreement (p0077, buried at the end of the Indemnity section) is one-sided: it limits TrueLink's liability to 12 months' hosting and support compensation, while Client's liability under the broad indemnity in Section 12a and elsewhere is entirely unlimited. A one-way cap protecting only the Vendor with the Customer uncapped is walk-away territory and fails the fallback element requiring mutuality. The cap also carves out only TrueLink's gross negligence and willful misconduct, with no carve-out for indemnification or confidentiality breaches. There is no exclusion of indirect or consequential damages anywhere in the document. We have taken the fallback position: the cap is made mutual and applied to the Agreement as a whole on the existing 12-month compensation basis, with indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct outside the cap. We have not pressed the preferred greater-of USD 1,000,000 formulation, the mutual consequential-damages exclusion or the data protection, fraud, IP-infringement and payment-obligation elements, which remain available in negotiation.

mappings.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.

proposal.summary: Make the 12-month cap mutual and carve out indemnities, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We made the cap mutual and applied it to the Agreement as a whole at twelve months' compensation, since as drafted only TrueLink is capped and Client's liability is unlimited. Indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct sit outside the cap; we can discuss our preferred greater-of USD 1,000,000 formulation if helpful.
